| 2026-07-29 | `src/data/reveal-family-aliases.ts` (new) | THR-844: added `REVEAL_FAMILY_ALIASES` — 67 authored reveal-family names mapped to the template-id prefixes they mean — plus `resolveRevealFamily()`. Unaliased families resolve to themselves. | A mark's `revealFamilies` was matched by raw `templateId.startsWith(family)`, so a family only worked if the author wrote a real id prefix. Measured against the shipped 672-template pool, 67 of 115 distinct literals matched **zero** templates and 42 of 136 entries named only dead ones — unrevealable by construction. The dead names are overwhelmingly thematic (`investigation`, `oracle`, `guild`, `duel`, `shrine`, `spy`), i.e. authors were writing a tag vocabulary against an engine that wanted prefixes; `investigation` alone is the corpus's most-used family at 65 uses and never fired. Population is pinned before anything is asserted about it (a guard over an empty corpus passes vacuously and reads exactly like one that works). **Falsified rather than assumed** — disabling alias resolution turns 70 of the 197 red. The upper bound matters as much as the lower: a family resolving to a quarter of the pool reveals on almost anything, which is as useless as revealing on nothing. |
